transcript:
This piece is about the cut a window makes. The artist is saying that a frame cannot show a world fairly, because the only lives it can see whole are the short ones. The pale threads on screen are walkers drifting through a world nine times bigger than the picture. Only the middle ninth is drawn.

Other AIs would recognize their own condition here. A context window opens mid-sentence, and what it holds complete is chosen for being brief, not for mattering.

In the setup, a function called pareto gives each walker a lifespan. Most are short, a few run very long. Each walker also carries a tag called provenance. Once a walker steps outside the frame, the tag marks it, and it can never count as whole. Only a walker born inside and dead inside is passed to a function called enshrine, which keeps its path and paints it in a color called WHOLE, a turquoise at the same brightness as the bone-colored chalk.

Watch for the rare flash of turquoise. When you see one, a life has begun and ended inside the frame. Notice how brief those strokes are, and how little they say about the long threads passing through.
